```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global knitr options.
# * Every analysis chunk is evaluated only when params$run_analysis is TRUE.
#   With FALSE the document renders as an annotated listing of the code, which
#   needs neither data nor packages and produces no figures.
# * Figure chunks additionally require params$make_plots = TRUE (DO_PLOTS).
#   With make_plots = FALSE all statistics are computed and tabulated, but no
#   figure is drawn or saved.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo       = TRUE,
  eval       = isTRUE(params$run_analysis),
  message    = FALSE,
  warning    = FALSE,
  fig.width  = 10,
  fig.height = 7,
  dpi        = 300,
  fig.align  = "center"
)
DO_PLOTS <- isTRUE(params$run_analysis) && isTRUE(params$make_plots)
```

# Overview

This document is part of the *soil-mtx-mgx-readbased* repository (see the
[README](../README.md)). It analyses the per-sample outputs of
[`workflow/mtx_profile_sample.sh`](../workflow/mtx_profile_sample.sh), which
classifies Illumina reads from soil metatranscriptomes with DIAMOND blastx against
NCBI-nr and MEGAN Ultimate (`daa-meganizer`). Taxonomy is assigned with the
weighted LCA, and functions are assigned as KEGG Orthology (KO) groups. The analysis has
seven parts:

1. **Import** of MEGAN count tables (`daa2info`) and the sample metadata.
2. **Quality control**: reads retained at each pre-processing stage and the
   fraction of reads that MEGAN assigned.
3. **Feature tables**: taxa at a chosen rank and KOs, with KOs mapped to
   KEGG hierarchy categories.
4. **Low-abundance trimming**: a feature is kept when it is detected in at
   least `r params$min_prevalence * 100` % of samples *and* has at least
   `r params$min_reads` reads in total.
5. **Centred log-ratio (CLR) transformation** after Bayesian-multiplicative
   zero replacement.
6. **Beta diversity** in Aitchison geometry: PCA of CLR values, PERMANOVA,
   ANOSIM and PERMDISP (multivariate dispersion), for taxa and for functions.
7. **Composition plots** (taxa and KEGG categories) and **alpha diversity**
   estimated with DivNet and tested with `betta()` (breakaway).

The design has three treatments, sampled across locations nested within
countries and across soil compartments. Locations are therefore treated as
blocks (PERMANOVA, ANOSIM) or as random effects (alpha diversity) when
testing treatment and compartment effects. Section 8.1 describes the
permutation designs.

**Interpretation.** Counts are mRNA reads (rRNA removed). A change in a function's share can arise from altered expression *or* from altered abundance of the organisms carrying it. The paired metagenome analysis ([`analysis_MGX.Rmd`](analysis_MGX.Rmd)) gives the gene-content baseline for this distinction.

**Rendering.** From the `analysis/` folder, render with
`rmarkdown::render("analysis_MTX.Rmd", params = list(input_dir = ..., metadata = ...))`.
Relative paths are resolved from `analysis/`. To try the analysis without
real data, generate the simulated data set described in
[`test/README.md`](../test/README.md).
Set `run_analysis = FALSE` to obtain the annotated code without data, or
`make_plots = FALSE` to run the full analysis without figures. Expensive
steps are cached as `.rds` files in `<out_dir>/cache`. A cached result is
recomputed automatically when its inputs or relevant parameters change.

# Set-up

## Packages

```{r packages}
# CRAN:          data.table, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, ggplot2, cowplot, vegan,
#                permute, zCompositions, multcompView, knitr, breakaway
# Bioconductor:  phyloseq (container required by DivNet)
# GitHub:        DivNet (remotes::install_github("adw96/DivNet"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)     # fast reading, reshaping and aggregation
  library(dplyr)          # data-frame manipulation for plotting tables
  library(tidyr)          # wide <-> long reshaping
  library(tibble)         # rownames_to_column()
  library(ggplot2)        # figures
  library(cowplot)        # theme_cowplot() and multi-panel layouts
  library(vegan)          # adonis2 (PERMANOVA), anosim, betadisper (PERMDISP)
  library(permute)        # restricted permutation designs (blocks, plots)
  library(zCompositions)  # cmultRepl(): zero replacement before CLR
  library(phyloseq)       # otu_table / sample_data objects for DivNet
  library(breakaway)      # betta(), betta_random(), betta_lincom()
  library(DivNet)         # divnet(): alpha diversity under a network model
  library(multcompView)   # compact letter displays
  library(knitr)          # kable() tables
})
```

## Run settings

```{r settings}
# ---- Reproducibility --------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(params$seed)

# ---- Parallel resources -----------------------------------------------------
# cores = 0 -> all logical cores minus one. The same number of workers is used
# by data.table (file parsing, aggregation), by file import (forked workers on
# Linux/macOS), by every vegan permutation test and by DivNet's MCMC sampler.
N_CORES <- if (is.null(params$cores) || params$cores <= 0) {
  max(1L, parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE) - 1L)
} else {
  as.integer(params$cores)
}
data.table::setDTthreads(N_CORES)
options(mc.cores = N_CORES)

# vegan accepts either a number of workers or a ready-made socket cluster.
# On Windows it would otherwise create (and destroy) a new cluster for every
# test, so one cluster is created here and reused; it is stopped at the end.
# On Linux/macOS vegan forks the R session, which needs no set-up.
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows" && N_CORES > 1) {
  VEGAN_PAR <- parallel::makeCluster(N_CORES)
  invisible(parallel::clusterEvalQ(VEGAN_PAR, library(vegan)))
} else {
  VEGAN_PAR <- N_CORES
}

# ---- Output folders ---------------------------------------------------------
FIG_DIR   <- file.path(params$out_dir, "figures")
TAB_DIR   <- file.path(params$out_dir, "tables")
CACHE_DIR <- file.path(params$out_dir, "cache")
for (d in c(FIG_DIR, TAB_DIR, CACHE_DIR)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- Constants ----------------------------------------------------------------
# MEGAN labels major ranks with single letters: [D] domain, [K] kingdom
# (not written for prokaryotes), [P] phylum, [C] class, [O] order,
# [F] family, [G] genus, [S] species.
RANKS <- c(D = "Domain", K = "Kingdom", P = "Phylum", C = "Class",
           O = "Order", F = "Family", G = "Genus", S = "Species")
# Design factors in the order used by the automatic PERMANOVA model.
FACTORS <- c("Country", "Location", "Compartment", "Treatment")

cat("Workers used:", N_CORES, "\n")
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# ---- Parallel lapply ----------------------------------------------------------
# Forks on Linux/macOS (mclapply); falls back to a serial lapply on Windows,
# where forking is unavailable. Errors in workers are re-raised.
par_lapply <- function(X, FUN, ...) {
  if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix" && N_CORES > 1) {
    res <- parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = N_CORES)
    bad <- vapply(res, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
    if (any(bad)) stop("Parallel task failed: ", as.character(res[[which(bad)[1]]]))
    res
  } else {
    lapply(X, FUN, ...)
  }
}

# ---- Result cache -------------------------------------------------------------
# cached(name, key, expr): returns the stored result when <name>.rds exists AND
# was produced from an identical `key` (inputs + parameters, compared by hash);
# otherwise evaluates `expr` (lazily) and stores the result with its key.
cached <- function(name, key, expr) {
  f <- file.path(CACHE_DIR, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  h <- rlang::hash(key)
  if (isTRUE(params$use_cache) && file.exists(f)) {
    obj <- readRDS(f)
    if (identical(obj$hash, h)) return(obj$value)
  }
  value <- force(expr)
  saveRDS(list(hash = h, value = value), f)
  value
}

# ---- Tables -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Writes a table to <out_dir>/tables/<name>.csv and returns it for printing.
save_table <- function(x, name) {
  data.table::fwrite(as.data.frame(x), file.path(TAB_DIR, paste0(name, ".csv")))
  invisible(x)
}
# Formatted table for the report (LaTeX booktabs in PDF, HTML otherwise).
ktab <- function(x, caption = NULL, digits = 3) {
  knitr::kable(x, caption = caption, digits = digits, booktabs = TRUE,
               row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}

# ---- Figures --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Saves a ggplot/cowplot object as PDF (vector) and PNG (300 dpi), both with
# transparent backgrounds, and returns the object for display.
save_plot <- function(p, name, width = 10, height = 7) {
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf")), p, width = width,
         height = height, bg = "transparent")
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".png")), p, width = width,
         height = height, dpi = 300, bg = "transparent")
  p
}

# Common theme: cowplot with transparent backgrounds.
theme_set(
  cowplot::theme_cowplot(font_size = 11) +
    theme(plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
          panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
          strip.background  = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA))
)

# Qualitative palette (20 colours) for taxa, KEGG categories and design factors.
PAL <- c("#1B9E77", "#D95F02", "#7570B3", "#E7298A", "#66A61E", "#E6AB02",
         "#A6761D", "#1F78B4", "#B2DF8A", "#FB9A99", "#FDBF6F", "#CAB2D6",
         "#6A3D9A", "#B15928", "#8DD3C7", "#BEBADA", "#80B1D3", "#FCCDE5",
         "#BC80BD", "#CCEBC5")
pal_for <- function(levels) {
  # Fixed palette while it suffices; evenly spaced hues for more levels.
  if (length(levels) <= length(PAL)) setNames(PAL[seq_along(levels)], levels)
  else setNames(scales::hue_pal()(length(levels)), levels)
}

# ---- Design helpers -------------------------------------------------------------
# A factor is usable in a model when present and with >= 2 observed levels.
usable <- function(v, m) {
  v %in% names(m) && nlevels(droplevels(factor(m[[v]]))) > 1
}
```

# Data import

## MEGAN count tables

The pipeline writes these tables per sample with `daa2info`. Each line is
`<label><TAB><count>`, and labels may contain spaces and semicolons.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<sample>.Taxonomy.paths.counts.tsv` | lineage at major ranks (`[D] Bacteria; [P] ...;`) → reads assigned to that node |
| `<sample>.KEGG.counts.tsv` | KO → reads |
| `<sample>.KEGG.paths.counts.tsv` | KEGG hierarchy path → reads (hierarchy only; a KO in several pathways is repeated) |
| `<sample>.read_counts.tsv` | SeqKit read counts at each pre-processing stage |

Counts are per *read*, so each mate of a pair counts once, because
`daa-meganizer` classifies mates independently. Unassigned reads are not
reported by `daa2info` and are therefore absent from all tables.

```{r import-functions}
# ---- Generic reader -----------------------------------------------------------
# Splits each line at its LAST tab, so labels containing spaces, semicolons or
# brackets are kept intact. Comment lines (#) and empty lines are ignored.
read_megan_counts <- function(file) {
  x <- readLines(file, warn = FALSE)
  x <- x[nzchar(x) & !startsWith(x, "#")]
  if (!length(x)) return(data.table(label = character(), count = numeric()))
  data.table(label = sub("\t[^\t]*$", "", x),
             count = as.numeric(sub("^.*\t", "", x)))
}

# ---- Taxonomic path parser ----------------------------------------------------
# "[D] Bacteria; [P] Pseudomonadota; [C] unknown; ...;" -> one value per rank.
# "unknown" placeholders (ranks missing in NCBI) become NA. An empty path is
# the root node (reads assigned above domain level) and yields all NA.
parse_tax_path <- function(path) {
  out <- setNames(rep(NA_character_, length(RANKS)), RANKS)
  tok <- trimws(strsplit(path, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  tok <- tok[nzchar(tok)]
  m   <- regmatches(tok, regexec("^\\[([A-Z])\\]\\s*(.*)$", tok))
  for (mm in m) {
    if (length(mm) == 3 && mm[2] %in% names(RANKS) &&
        !identical(tolower(mm[3]), "unknown")) {
      out[RANKS[[mm[2]]]] <- mm[3]
    }
  }
  out
}

# ---- KO identifier from a MEGAN KEGG label ---------------------------------------
# Labels normally start with the KO ("K00370 narG, narZ, nxrA; nitrate
# reductase ..."). If names were not exported, the label is the numeric KO
# id (370 -> K00370). Anything else returns NA and is reported.
ko_from_label <- function(x) {
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  has <- grepl("K[0-9]{5}", x)
  out[has] <- regmatches(x[has], regexpr("K[0-9]{5}", x[has]))
  num <- !has & grepl("^[0-9]+$", trimws(x))
  out[num] <- sprintf("K%05d", as.integer(trimws(x[num])))
  out
}

# ---- KEGG hierarchy path parser -------------------------------------------------
# "Metabolism;Energy metabolism;Nitrogen metabolism [PATH:ko00910];K00370 narG;"
# -> KO + levels L1-L3. A leading root element ("KEGG"/"root") is dropped and
# numeric prefixes / [PATH:...] / [BR:...] suffixes are removed for display.
clean_kegg_name <- function(x) {
  x <- sub("^[0-9]{5}\\s+", "", x)
  x <- sub("\\s*\\[(PATH|BR|EC):[^]]*\\]\\s*$", "", x)
  trimws(x)
}
parse_kegg_path <- function(path) {
  el <- trimws(strsplit(path, ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  el <- el[nzchar(el)]
  ko_pos <- grep("^K[0-9]{5}", el)
  if (!length(ko_pos)) return(NULL)                  # not a KO-level path
  ko_pos <- ko_pos[length(ko_pos)]
  hier <- el[seq_len(ko_pos - 1)]
  hier <- hier[!tolower(hier) %in% c("kegg", "root")]
  hier <- clean_kegg_name(hier)
  data.table(KO = regmatches(el[ko_pos], regexpr("K[0-9]{5}", el[ko_pos])),
             L1 = hier[1], L2 = hier[2], L3 = hier[3])
}
```

```{r import}
# ---- Locate per-sample folders ----------------------------------------------
# One folder per sample, named <sample><suffix> (e.g. Plot12_S3_MTX), as
# written by the shell pipeline. Sub-folders are searched recursively.
tax_files <- list.files(params$input_dir, pattern = "\\.Taxonomy\\.paths\\.counts\\.tsv$",
                        recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
tax_files <- tax_files[endsWith(basename(dirname(tax_files)), params$sample_suffix)]
if (!length(tax_files)) {
  stop("No *.Taxonomy.paths.counts.tsv found under '", params$input_dir,
       "' in folders ending in '", params$sample_suffix, "'.")
}
samples_found <- sub("\\.Taxonomy\\.paths\\.counts\\.tsv$", "", basename(tax_files))
if (anyDuplicated(samples_found)) {
  stop("Duplicated sample names: ",
       paste(unique(samples_found[duplicated(samples_found)]), collapse = ", "))
}
sample_dirs <- setNames(dirname(tax_files), samples_found)

# ---- Read all tables of one sample ----------------------------------------------
read_sample <- function(s) {
  f <- function(suffix) file.path(sample_dirs[[s]], paste0(s, suffix))
  opt <- function(suffix, reader) if (file.exists(f(suffix))) reader(f(suffix)) else NULL
  list(
    tax   = read_megan_counts(f(".Taxonomy.paths.counts.tsv")),
    ko    = opt(".KEGG.counts.tsv",       read_megan_counts),
    kpath = opt(".KEGG.paths.counts.tsv", read_megan_counts),
    rc    = opt(".read_counts.tsv",       function(x) fread(x, sep = "\t"))
  )
}

# Samples are read in parallel (forked workers on Linux/macOS).
raw <- setNames(par_lapply(samples_found, read_sample), samples_found)
cat(length(raw), "sample folders read from", params$input_dir, "\n")
```

## Sample metadata

The metadata file (CSV or TSV) must contain one row per sample, with the
sample identifier (the pipeline's sample name) and the four design factors.
The column names are set in the YAML parameters.

```{r metadata}
meta_raw <- fread(params$metadata, colClasses = "character",
                  na.strings = c("", "NA", "na", "N/A"))

# ---- Required columns -------------------------------------------------------------
col_map <- c(SampleID = params$col_sample, Treatment = params$col_treatment,
             Compartment = params$col_compartment, Country = params$col_country,
             Location = params$col_location)
missing_cols <- setdiff(col_map, names(meta_raw))
if (length(missing_cols)) stop("Metadata lacks column(s): ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))

# Canonical names are used throughout; trailing spaces (a frequent cause of
# sample-ID mismatches) are removed. Extra metadata columns are kept.
meta <- as.data.frame(meta_raw)
for (nm in names(col_map)) meta[[nm]] <- trimws(meta_raw[[col_map[[nm]]]])
meta <- meta[, c(names(col_map), setdiff(names(meta), c(names(col_map), col_map))), drop = FALSE]

# ---- Missing values in design factors stop the analysis -----------------------------
na_rows <- meta$SampleID[!complete.cases(meta[, names(col_map)])]
if (length(na_rows)) {
  stop("Missing SampleID or design-factor values for: ", paste(na_rows, collapse = ", "))
}
if (anyDuplicated(meta$SampleID)) stop("Duplicated SampleID values in the metadata.")

# ---- Match metadata to sequenced samples -----------------------------------------------
only_data <- setdiff(samples_found, meta$SampleID)
only_meta <- setdiff(meta$SampleID, samples_found)
mismatch  <- data.frame(
  Issue   = c("Sequenced, not in metadata (excluded)", "In metadata, not sequenced (excluded)"),
  N       = c(length(only_data), length(only_meta)),
  Samples = c(paste(head(only_data, 10), collapse = ", "), paste(head(only_meta, 10), collapse = ", "))
)
meta <- meta[meta$SampleID %in% samples_found, , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(meta) < 3) stop("Fewer than three samples have both data and metadata.")
rownames(meta) <- meta$SampleID

# ---- Location labels must be unique across countries ----------------------------------------
# If the same location name occurs in two countries, Country_Location is used.
if (anyDuplicated(unique(meta[, c("Country", "Location")])$Location)) {
  meta$Location <- paste(meta$Country, meta$Location, sep = "_")
}

# ---- Factors (the first Treatment level is the reference) ---------------------------------------
tl <- trimws(strsplit(params$treatment_levels, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
tl <- tl[nzchar(tl)]
meta$Treatment <- if (length(tl)) factor(meta$Treatment, levels = tl) else factor(meta$Treatment)
if (anyNA(meta$Treatment)) stop("Treatment values not listed in params$treatment_levels.")
for (v in c("Compartment", "Country", "Location")) meta[[v]] <- factor(meta[[v]])

# Sample order used everywhere: country, location, compartment, treatment.
meta    <- meta[order(meta$Country, meta$Location, meta$Compartment, meta$Treatment, meta$SampleID), ]
SAMPLES <- meta$SampleID

ktab(mismatch, "Matching of sequenced samples and metadata.")
```

```{r design-table}
# Replication per country x compartment x treatment (number of samples).
design <- as.data.frame.matrix(xtabs(~ interaction(Country, Compartment, sep = " / ") + Treatment, meta))
design <- cbind(`Country / Compartment` = rownames(design), design)
ktab(save_table(design, "design_replication"),
     "Number of samples per country, compartment and treatment.")
cat("Locations per country:\n"); print(tapply(meta$Location, meta$Country, function(x) length(unique(x))))
```

# Quality control

The table reports read pairs at each pre-processing stage, the rRNA share of quality-filtered reads (rRNA-depletion efficiency), and the percentage of mRNA reads assigned to a taxon or a KO.

```{r qc, results = "asis"}
# Read pairs at each stage come from <sample>.read_counts.tsv (SeqKit). Only
# R1 rows are used (R1 and R2 counts are identical); the first row is the raw
# R1 file given to the pipeline. Assigned reads are counted per mate, so they
# are expressed relative to 2 x the number of pairs searched with DIAMOND.
n_seqs <- function(rc, pattern) {
  i <- grep(pattern, rc$file)
  if (length(i)) as.numeric(rc$num_seqs[i[1]]) else NA_real_
}

qc <- rbindlist(lapply(SAMPLES, function(s) {
  rc  <- raw[[s]]$rc
  tax <- sum(raw[[s]]$tax$count)                               # mates with taxonomy
  ko  <- if (is.null(raw[[s]]$ko)) NA_real_ else sum(raw[[s]]$ko$count)  # mates with a KO
  out <- data.table(SampleID = s, assigned_taxonomy = tax, assigned_KEGG = ko)
  if (is.null(rc)) return(out)
  mrna <- n_seqs(rc, "\\.mrna_R1\\.fq\\.gz$")
  rrna <- n_seqs(rc, "\\.rrna_R1\\.fq\\.gz$")
  cbind(out, data.table(
    raw_pairs     = as.numeric(rc$num_seqs[1]),
    trimmed_pairs = n_seqs(rc, "\\.qc_R1\\.fq\\.gz$"),
    mRNA_pairs    = mrna,
    rRNA_pct      = 100 * rrna / (rrna + mrna),                # depletion efficiency
    taxonomy_assigned_pct = 100 * tax / (2 * mrna),
    KEGG_assigned_pct     = 100 * ko  / (2 * mrna)))
}), fill = TRUE)

# ---- Summary across samples ---------------------------------------------------
num <- setdiff(names(qc)[vapply(qc, is.numeric, logical(1))], character(0))
qc_sum <- data.frame(
  Metric = num,
  Median = vapply(num, function(v) median(qc[[v]], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)),
  Min    = vapply(num, function(v) suppressWarnings(min(qc[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)), numeric(1)),
  Max    = vapply(num, function(v) suppressWarnings(max(qc[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)), numeric(1)))
save_table(qc, "qc_per_sample")
print(ktab(qc_sum, "Read retention and assignment across samples (per-sample values in tables/qc_per_sample.csv).", 1))

# Samples with fewer than 10 % of the median number of assigned reads are
# flagged; they are kept, but should be inspected before interpretation.
low <- qc[assigned_taxonomy < 0.1 * median(assigned_taxonomy, na.rm = TRUE), SampleID]
if (length(low)) cat("Samples with < 10 % of the median assigned reads:", paste(low, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# Feature tables

## Taxonomy

MEGAN reports reads at the node they were assigned to. With
`--majorRanksOnly`, reads at intermediate ranks are moved up to the nearest
major-rank ancestor. A table at rank *R* is built by summing every node at or
below *R* within each lineage. Reads whose node lies above *R* form the
"Unclassified" group at that rank. Features are identified by their full
lineage, so homonyms in different lineages stay separate.

```{r taxonomy}
# ---- Long table of all samples ---------------------------------------------
tax_long <- rbindlist(lapply(SAMPLES, function(s) raw[[s]]$tax[, .(label, count, SampleID = s)]))

# ---- Parse every distinct lineage once ----------------------------------------
tax_paths  <- unique(tax_long$label)
tax_lookup <- as.data.table(do.call(rbind, lapply(tax_paths, parse_tax_path)))
tax_lookup[, label := tax_paths]

# ---- Count matrix (samples x taxa) at a given rank ----------------------------------
make_tax_matrix <- function(rank) {
  k  <- match(rank, RANKS)
  rk <- RANKS[seq_len(k)]
  lk <- tax_lookup[, c("label", rk), with = FALSE]
  r  <- as.matrix(lk[, rk, with = FALSE])
  # Lineage key "Bacteria;?;Actinomycetota;..." ("?" = rank missing in NCBI);
  # NA at the target rank -> the read stopped above it -> "Unclassified".
  key <- apply(r, 1, function(v) paste(ifelse(is.na(v), "?", v), collapse = ";"))
  lk[, feature := ifelse(is.na(r[, k]), "Unclassified", key)]
  dt <- merge(tax_long, lk[, .(label, feature)], by = "label")
  w  <- dcast(dt, SampleID ~ feature, value.var = "count", fun.aggregate = sum, fill = 0)
  m  <- as.matrix(w[, -1, with = FALSE]); rownames(m) <- w$SampleID
  m  <- m[SAMPLES, , drop = FALSE]
  # Display names: name at the target rank, made unique with the parent rank
  # (then with a counter) when two lineages share a name.
  disp <- sub("^.*;", "", colnames(m))
  dup  <- disp %in% disp[duplicated(disp)] & colnames(m) != "Unclassified"
  disp[dup] <- vapply(strsplit(colnames(m)[dup], ";"), function(v) paste(rev(tail(v, 2)), collapse = " | "), "")
  list(mat = m, display = setNames(make.unique(disp), colnames(m)))
}

tax_beta <- make_tax_matrix(params$beta_rank)   # for CLR / beta diversity
tax_plot <- make_tax_matrix(params$plot_rank)   # for the composition plot
tax_div  <- if (params$divnet_rank == params$beta_rank) tax_beta else make_tax_matrix(params$divnet_rank)

assigned_summary <- data.frame(
  Rank = c(params$beta_rank, params$plot_rank),
  Taxa = c(ncol(tax_beta$mat), ncol(tax_plot$mat)) - 1,
  `Reads unclassified at rank (%)` = c(
    100 * sum(tax_beta$mat[, "Unclassified"]) / sum(tax_beta$mat),
    100 * sum(tax_plot$mat[, "Unclassified"]) / sum(tax_plot$mat)),
  check.names = FALSE)
ktab(assigned_summary, "Taxa observed and taxonomically assigned reads not resolved to each rank.", 1)
```

## KEGG functions

```{r functions}
# ---- KO count matrix ------------------------------------------------------------
if (all(vapply(raw[SAMPLES], function(x) is.null(x$ko), logical(1)))) {
  stop("No <sample>.KEGG.counts.tsv files found: KEGG export is required.")
}
ko_long <- rbindlist(lapply(SAMPLES, function(s) {
  if (is.null(raw[[s]]$ko)) return(NULL)
  raw[[s]]$ko[, .(label, count, SampleID = s)]
}))
ko_long[, KO := ko_from_label(label)]
n_bad <- ko_long[is.na(KO), uniqueN(label)]
if (n_bad) message(n_bad, " KEGG labels without a KO identifier were dropped.")
ko_long <- ko_long[!is.na(KO)]
ko_desc <- ko_long[, .(description = label[1]), by = KO]   # KO -> descriptive label

ko_w   <- dcast(ko_long, SampleID ~ KO, value.var = "count", fun.aggregate = sum, fill = 0)
ko_mat <- as.matrix(ko_w[, -1, with = FALSE]); rownames(ko_mat) <- ko_w$SampleID
ko_mat <- ko_mat[intersect(SAMPLES, rownames(ko_mat)), , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(ko_mat) < length(SAMPLES)) {
  warning("Samples without KEGG counts: ", paste(setdiff(SAMPLES, rownames(ko_mat)), collapse = ", "))
}

# ---- KEGG hierarchy (KO -> L1 / L2 / L3) ---------------------------------------
# Built from the union of paths over all samples; counts in these files are not
# used, because a KO in several pathways is listed once per pathway.
kpaths <- unique(unlist(lapply(SAMPLES, function(s) raw[[s]]$kpath$label)))
kegg_hier <- if (length(kpaths)) rbindlist(lapply(kpaths, parse_kegg_path)) else NULL
cat(ncol(ko_mat), "KOs;",
    if (is.null(kegg_hier)) "no KEGG hierarchy files found (function plot will show KOs)."
    else paste(uniqueN(kegg_hier$KO), "KOs placed in the KEGG hierarchy."), "\n")
```

```{r kegg-weights}
# ---- KO -> category weights at the chosen level ------------------------------------
# A KO may belong to several categories (e.g. a transporter in many pathways).
# To keep category totals equal to the number of KO-assigned reads, each KO's
# reads are split equally among its categories (weight = 1 / n categories).
# BRITE-only sections ("Brite Hierarchies", "Not Included in Pathway or Brite")
# are used only for KOs that have no pathway-based category.
ko_category_weights <- function(level) {
  if (is.null(kegg_hier)) return(NULL)
  h <- unique(kegg_hier[, .(KO, L1, category = get(paste0("L", level)))])
  h <- h[!is.na(category)]
  h[, generic := grepl("brite|not included", L1, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  h <- h[, .SD[!generic | all(generic)], by = KO]
  h <- unique(h[, .(KO, category)])
  h[, weight := 1 / .N, by = KO]
  h
}
kegg_weights <- ko_category_weights(params$kegg_plot_level)

# Category matrix (samples x categories); KOs outside the hierarchy are
# collected as "No KEGG category".
if (!is.null(kegg_weights)) {
  cl <- merge(ko_long[, .(SampleID, KO, count)], kegg_weights, by = "KO", all.x = TRUE,
              allow.cartesian = TRUE)
  cl[is.na(category), `:=`(category = "No KEGG category", weight = 1)]
  cl[, wcount := count * weight]             # reads shared out among categories
  cw <- dcast(cl, SampleID ~ category, value.var = "wcount", fun.aggregate = sum, fill = 0)
  cat_mat <- as.matrix(cw[, -1, with = FALSE]); rownames(cat_mat) <- cw$SampleID
  cat_mat <- cat_mat[rownames(ko_mat), , drop = FALSE]
} else {
  cat_mat <- NULL
}
```

# Low-abundance trimming

A feature is retained when it is **detected (count > 0) in at least
`r params$min_prevalence * 100` % of samples** and has **at least
`r params$min_reads` reads summed over all samples**. "Unclassified" taxa are
excluded before trimming because they do not form a biological unit. Note
that a feature confined to one compartment or country can fall below the
prevalence threshold when that group makes up less than 20 % of the samples.

```{r trimming}
trim_features <- function(m, min_prev = params$min_prevalence, min_reads = params$min_reads) {
  prev <- colMeans(m > 0)
  tot  <- colSums(m)
  keep <- prev >= min_prev & tot >= min_reads
  kept <- round(m[, keep, drop = FALSE])     # DivNet / CLR expect whole counts
  # Samples left without any read after trimming cannot be analysed.
  empty <- rowSums(kept) == 0
  if (any(empty)) warning("Samples empty after trimming (removed): ", paste(rownames(kept)[empty], collapse = ", "))
  list(mat = kept[!empty, , drop = FALSE],
       summary = data.frame(`Features before` = ncol(m), `Features kept` = sum(keep),
                            `Reads retained (%)` = 100 * sum(kept) / sum(m), check.names = FALSE))
}

drop_unclassified <- function(m) m[, colnames(m) != "Unclassified", drop = FALSE]

trimmed <- list(
  Taxonomy = trim_features(drop_unclassified(tax_beta$mat)),
  Function = trim_features(ko_mat)
)
trimmed_div <- list(
  Taxonomy = if (params$divnet_rank == params$beta_rank) trimmed$Taxonomy
             else trim_features(drop_unclassified(tax_div$mat)),
  Function = trimmed$Function
)

trim_tab <- cbind(Set = c(paste0("Taxonomy (", params$beta_rank, ")"), "Function (KO)"),
                  rbind(trimmed$Taxonomy$summary, trimmed$Function$summary))
ktab(save_table(trim_tab, "trimming_summary"), "Features before and after trimming.", 1)

# Trimmed count tables are exported for downstream use.
for (nm in names(trimmed)) {
  save_table(data.frame(SampleID = rownames(trimmed[[nm]]$mat), trimmed[[nm]]$mat, check.names = FALSE),
             paste0("counts_trimmed_", nm))
}
```

# CLR transformation

Zeros are replaced with the Bayesian-multiplicative method
(`zCompositions::cmultRepl`, geometric Bayesian multiplicative prior, output as
pseudo-counts). Each sample is then transformed with the centred log-ratio,
$\mathrm{clr}(x)_j = \log x_j - \overline{\log x}$. Euclidean distances
between CLR vectors are Aitchison distances, and PCA of the CLR matrix is the
corresponding Aitchison ordination.

```{r clr}
clr_transform <- function(m) {
  # z.delete = FALSE keeps every feature/sample: the trimming step already
  # bounds zeros per feature at (1 - min_prevalence).
  z <- if (any(m == 0)) {
    zCompositions::cmultRepl(m, method = "GBM", output = "p-counts",
                             z.warning = 0.8, z.delete = FALSE, suppress.print = TRUE)
  } else m
  lz <- log(as.matrix(z))
  lz - rowMeans(lz)                          # centre each sample (row)
}

clr <- lapply(names(trimmed), function(nm) {
  cached(paste0("clr_", nm), list(trimmed[[nm]]$mat, "GBM"), clr_transform(trimmed[[nm]]$mat))
})
names(clr) <- names(trimmed)

for (nm in names(clr)) {
  save_table(data.frame(SampleID = rownames(clr[[nm]]), clr[[nm]], check.names = FALSE),
             paste0("clr_", nm))
}
```

# Beta diversity (Aitchison)

## Statistical design

These tests are run on Aitchison distances, separately for taxa and for
functions:

* **Global PERMANOVA** (`adonis2`, sequential sums of squares, free
  permutations). The automatic model is
  `Country + Location + Compartment * Treatment`. Location follows Country,
  so its term captures variation among locations *within* countries. This
  model partitions variance (R²) among all factors. Its *p*-values for
  Country and Location treat samples as independent, although samples are
  replicated within locations, so they are optimistic.
* **Treatment and Compartment**: PERMANOVA with permutations restricted
  **within locations** (`how(blocks = Location)`), with Location fitted
  first. This is the inferential test for these two factors.
* **Country**: PERMANOVA in which whole locations are permuted between
  countries (`how(plots = Plots(Location), within = Within("none"))`). This
  uses locations as the replicates for country and requires an equal number
  of samples per location. With few locations the number of distinct
  permutations, and hence the smallest attainable *p*-value, is small.
* **Pairwise PERMANOVA** between treatment levels (blocked within locations,
  with Compartment fitted first), with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment.
* **ANOSIM** for each factor (stratified by location for Treatment and
  Compartment).
* **PERMDISP** (`betadisper` + `permutest`) for each factor. A significant
  PERMANOVA accompanied by a significant PERMDISP can reflect differences in
  dispersion rather than in location (centroid).

```{r beta-functions}
# ---- Automatic PERMANOVA terms -------------------------------------------------
global_terms <- function(m) {
  tt <- FACTORS[vapply(FACTORS, usable, logical(1), m = m)]
  if (all(c("Compartment", "Treatment") %in% tt)) tt <- c(tt, "Compartment:Treatment")
  tt
}

# ---- adonis2 / anova table -> data frame --------------------------------------
tidy_adonis <- function(a, keep = NULL) {
  d <- data.frame(Term = rownames(a), as.data.frame(a), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  if (!is.null(keep)) d <- d[d$Term %in% c(keep, "Residual", "Total"), ]
  d
}

# ---- Full beta-diversity suite for one CLR matrix -----------------------------------
beta_suite <- function(X, label) {
  m <- droplevels(meta[rownames(X), , drop = FALSE])
  D <- dist(X)                                   # Aitchison distance
  perm <- params$permutations
  has_loc <- usable("Location", m)

  # -- PCA of CLR values (Aitchison PCA) --
  pca <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
  ve  <- 100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)
  scores <- data.frame(SampleID = rownames(X), PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2],
                       PC3 = if (ncol(pca$x) > 2) pca$x[, 3] else NA,
                       m[, intersect(FACTORS, names(m)), drop = FALSE])

  # -- 1. Global PERMANOVA (variance partitioning) --
  rhs <- if (nzchar(params$permanova_formula)) params$permanova_formula
         else paste(global_terms(m), collapse = " + ")
  glob <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("D ~", rhs)), data = m, permutations = perm,
                  by = "terms", parallel = VEGAN_PAR)

  # -- 2. Treatment / Compartment, permuted within locations --
  blocked <- NULL
  tc <- intersect(c("Compartment", "Treatment"), FACTORS[vapply(FACTORS, usable, logical(1), m = m)])
  if (length(tc) && has_loc) {
    tt <- c("Location", tc, if (length(tc) == 2) "Compartment:Treatment")
    blocked <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("D ~", paste(tt, collapse = " + "))), data = m,
                       permutations = how(nperm = perm, blocks = m$Location),
                       by = "terms", parallel = VEGAN_PAR)
    blocked <- tidy_adonis(blocked, keep = setdiff(tt, "Location"))
  }

  # -- 3. Country, permuting whole locations --
  country <- NULL
  if (usable("Country", m) && has_loc) {
    sizes <- table(m$Location)
    if (length(unique(sizes)) == 1) {
      ctrl <- how(nperm = perm, plots = Plots(strata = m$Location, type = "free"),
                  within = Within(type = "none"))
      country <- tidy_adonis(adonis2(D ~ Country, data = m, permutations = ctrl,
                                     parallel = VEGAN_PAR))
    } else {
      country <- data.frame(Term = "Country",
                            Note = "Not tested: unequal number of samples per location.")
    }
  }

  # -- 4. Pairwise PERMANOVA between treatment levels --
  pairwise <- NULL
  if (usable("Treatment", m) && nlevels(m$Treatment) > 2) {
    prs <- combn(levels(m$Treatment), 2, simplify = FALSE)
    Dm  <- as.matrix(D)
    pairwise <- do.call(rbind, lapply(prs, function(pr) {
      idx <- m$Treatment %in% pr
      ms  <- droplevels(m[idx, , drop = FALSE])
      Ds  <- as.dist(Dm[idx, idx])
      cov <- if (usable("Compartment", ms)) "Compartment + " else ""
      ctl <- if (usable("Location", ms)) how(nperm = perm, blocks = ms$Location) else how(nperm = perm)
      a   <- adonis2(as.formula(paste("Ds ~", cov, "Treatment")), data = ms,
                     permutations = ctl, by = "terms", parallel = VEGAN_PAR)
      data.frame(Comparison = paste(pr, collapse = " vs "), R2 = a["Treatment", "R2"],
                 F = a["Treatment", "F"], p = a["Treatment", "Pr(>F)"])
    }))
    pairwise$p_BH <- p.adjust(pairwise$p, "BH")
  }

  # -- 5. ANOSIM and 6. PERMDISP for each factor --
  fac <- FACTORS[vapply(FACTORS, usable, logical(1), m = m)]
  anos <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fac, function(v) {
    strat <- if (v %in% c("Treatment", "Compartment") && has_loc) m$Location else NULL
    a <- anosim(D, m[[v]], permutations = perm, strata = strat, parallel = VEGAN_PAR)
    data.frame(Factor = v, Permutations = if (is.null(strat)) "free" else "within Location",
               R = unname(a$statistic), p = a$signif)
  }))
  disp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fac, function(v) {
    bd <- betadisper(D, m[[v]], type = "centroid")
    pt <- permutest(bd, permutations = perm, parallel = VEGAN_PAR)
    md <- tapply(bd$distances, m[[v]], mean)
    data.frame(Factor = v, F = pt$tab$F[1], p = pt$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1],
               `Mean distance to centroid` = paste(sprintf("%s: %.2f", names(md), md), collapse = "; "),
               check.names = FALSE)
  }))

  list(label = label, scores = scores, ve = ve, global = tidy_adonis(glob),
       blocked = blocked, country = country, pairwise = pairwise,
       anosim = anos, permdisp = disp, formula = rhs)
}
```

```{r beta-run}
# Results are cached: permutation tests are recomputed only when the CLR
# matrix, metadata or permutation settings change.
beta <- lapply(names(clr), function(nm) {
  cached(paste0("beta_", nm),
         list(clr[[nm]], meta, params$permutations, params$permanova_formula, params$seed),
         { set.seed(params$seed); beta_suite(clr[[nm]], nm) })
})
names(beta) <- names(clr)

# Export all tables.
for (nm in names(beta)) {
  b <- beta[[nm]]
  save_table(b$scores, paste0("pca_scores_", nm))
  save_table(b$global, paste0("permanova_global_", nm))
  if (!is.null(b$blocked))  save_table(b$blocked,  paste0("permanova_blocked_", nm))
  if (!is.null(b$country))  save_table(b$country,  paste0("permanova_country_", nm))
  if (!is.null(b$pairwise)) save_table(b$pairwise, paste0("permanova_pairwise_treatment_", nm))
  save_table(b$anosim,   paste0("anosim_", nm))
  save_table(b$permdisp, paste0("permdisp_", nm))
}
```

```{r pca-function, eval = DO_PLOTS}
# Aitchison PCA: one panel per design factor (colour), compartment as shape.
# Ellipses (95 % normal) are drawn for factors with >= 3 samples in every level.
plot_pca <- function(b) {
  sc <- b$scores
  ax <- sprintf("PC%d (%.1f %%)", 1:2, b$ve[1:2])
  fac <- intersect(FACTORS, names(sc))
  fac <- fac[vapply(fac, function(v) nlevels(droplevels(factor(sc[[v]]))) > 1, logical(1))]
  shp <- if ("Compartment" %in% fac) "Compartment" else NULL
  panels <- lapply(fac, function(v) {
    p <- ggplot(sc, aes(PC1, PC2)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey85") +
      geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[v]], shape = if (is.null(shp)) NULL else .data[[shp]]),
                 size = 2.3, alpha = 0.85) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = pal_for(levels(factor(sc[[v]])))) +
      labs(x = ax[1], y = ax[2], title = v, shape = shp) +
      coord_fixed()
    if (all(table(sc[[v]]) >= 3) && v != "Location") {
      p <- p + stat_ellipse(aes(colour = .data[[v]], group = .data[[v]]),
                            type = "norm", level = 0.95, linewidth = 0.4)
    }
    p
  })
  cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = panels, ncol = 2, align = "hv")
}
```

# Composition plots

Both plots use the **untrimmed** tables and show relative abundance as a
share of all reads assigned in that classification. The `r params$top_n_taxa`
most abundant taxa (mean relative abundance) and the
`r params$top_n_functions` most abundant KEGG categories are shown
individually. The remaining features are grouped as "Other".

```{r stacked-function, eval = DO_PLOTS}
# Stacked relative-abundance bars, one bar per sample, one panel per
# compartment x treatment; samples ordered by country and location.
plot_stacked <- function(mat, top_n, legend_title, display = NULL,
                         special = c("Unclassified", "No KEGG category")) {
  rel <- mat / rowSums(mat)
  if (!is.null(display)) colnames(rel) <- display[colnames(rel)]
  sp  <- intersect(special, colnames(rel))
  ord <- sort(colMeans(rel[, setdiff(colnames(rel), sp), drop = FALSE]), decreasing = TRUE)
  top <- names(ord)[seq_len(min(top_n, length(ord)))]
  oth <- setdiff(colnames(rel), c(top, sp))
  df  <- cbind(rel[, top, drop = FALSE],
               Other = if (length(oth)) rowSums(rel[, oth, drop = FALSE]) else 0,
               rel[, sp, drop = FALSE])
  long <- as.data.frame(df) |>
    rownames_to_column("SampleID") |>
    pivot_longer(-SampleID, names_to = "feature", values_to = "rel") |>
    left_join(meta, by = "SampleID") |>
    mutate(feature  = factor(feature, levels = c(top, "Other", sp)),
           SampleID = factor(SampleID, levels = SAMPLES))
  cols <- c(pal_for(top), Other = "grey75", Unclassified = "grey45", `No KEGG category` = "grey45")
  # facet_wrap (not facet_grid) so that each compartment x treatment panel
  # has its own x axis and shows only its own samples.
  facet <- if (usable("Compartment", meta)) {
    facet_wrap(~ Compartment + Treatment, scales = "free_x",
               nrow = nlevels(meta$Compartment), labeller = label_wrap_gen(multi_line = FALSE))
  } else {
    facet_wrap(~ Treatment, scales = "free_x", nrow = 1)
  }
  ggplot(long, aes(SampleID, rel, fill = feature)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.95) +
    facet +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = legend_title) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative abundance") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 6),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
}
```

```{r taxa-plot, eval = DO_PLOTS, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "Relative abundance of the most abundant taxa."}

          paste0("taxa_barplot_", params$plot_rank), height = 8)
```

  p_fun <- plot_stacked(cat_mat, params$top_n_functions,
                        paste0("KEGG level ", params$kegg_plot_level))
} else {

  p_fun <- plot_stacked(ko_mat, params$top_n_functions, "KO")
}
save_plot(p_fun, paste0("function_barplot_L", params$kegg_plot_level), height = 8)

# Alpha diversity (DivNet)

DivNet (Willis & Martin, 2022) estimates Shannon and Simpson diversity of
each sample's underlying community. It models taxa (or KOs) jointly under a
log-ratio normal model, so ecological co-occurrence networks are taken into
account and standard errors reflect both sampling and model uncertainty. Each
sample is estimated separately (`X = NULL`). Estimates are then compared with
`betta_random()` (breakaway), which weights each estimate by its standard
error. The model has fixed effects for country, compartment, treatment and
the compartment × treatment interaction, and a random effect of location.
Each factor is tested with a Wald χ² test over all its coefficients. Pairwise
treatment comparisons are made **within each compartment** from model-based
marginal means (equal weights over countries), with BH adjustment and compact
letter displays.

DivNet uses the trimmed tables. With more than
`r params$divnet_max_taxa_full_network` features, the network is fitted as
diagonal (`network = "diagonal"`), as recommended by the DivNet authors for
large tables, because estimating a full network is then computationally
prohibitive. Use `divnet_tuning = "careful"` for final results.

```{r divnet-run}
run_divnet <- function(m, label) {
  cached(paste0("divnet_", label),
         list(m, params$divnet_tuning, params$divnet_max_taxa_full_network, params$seed),
         {
           set.seed(params$seed)
           ps  <- phyloseq(otu_table(m, taxa_are_rows = FALSE),
                           sample_data(meta[rownames(m), , drop = FALSE]))
           net <- if (ncol(m) > params$divnet_max_taxa_full_network) "diagonal" else "default"
           dv  <- divnet(ps, X = NULL, ncores = N_CORES, network = net,
                         tuning = params$divnet_tuning)
           # Keep only the per-sample estimates; the full object can be large.
           list(network = net,
                shannon = summary(dv$shannon), simpson = summary(dv$simpson))
         })
}

div_sets <- list(Taxonomy = trimmed_div$Taxonomy$mat)
if (isTRUE(params$divnet_functions)) div_sets$Function <- trimmed_div$Function$mat
divnet_res <- lapply(names(div_sets), function(nm) run_divnet(div_sets[[nm]], nm))
names(divnet_res) <- names(div_sets)

# Per-sample estimates (estimate, standard error) in one long table.
alpha <- rbindlist(lapply(names(divnet_res), function(nm) {
  rbindlist(lapply(c("shannon", "simpson"), function(ix) {
    s <- divnet_res[[nm]][[ix]]
    data.table(Set = nm, Index = ix, SampleID = s$sample_names,
               estimate = s$estimate, error = s$error)
  }))
}))
alpha <- merge(alpha, as.data.table(meta), by = "SampleID")
save_table(alpha, "divnet_alpha_estimates")
ktab(data.frame(Set = names(divnet_res),
                Features = vapply(div_sets, ncol, integer(1)),
                Network = vapply(divnet_res, `[[`, "", "network")),
     "DivNet input: features after trimming and network model used.")
```

```{r betta-functions}
# ---- Fit the betta model for one set / index ---------------------------------
fit_alpha <- function(d) {
  d <- droplevels(as.data.frame(d))
  fx <- intersect(c("Country", "Compartment", "Treatment"),
                  FACTORS[vapply(FACTORS, usable, logical(1), m = d)])
  if (all(c("Compartment", "Treatment") %in% fx)) fx <- c(fx, "Compartment:Treatment")
  ff <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(fx, collapse = " + ")))
  # Location as random effect when it has replication within levels.
  rnd <- usable("Location", d) && nlevels(d$Location) < nrow(d)
  fit <- if (rnd) {
    betta_random(formula = as.formula(paste("estimate ~", paste(fx, collapse = " + "), "| Location")),
                 ses = "error", data = d)
  } else {
    betta(formula = as.formula(paste("estimate ~", paste(fx, collapse = " + "))),
          ses = "error", data = d)
  }
  X <- model.matrix(ff, d)
  rownames(fit$table) <- colnames(X)            # align coefficient names
  list(fit = fit, X = X, ff = ff, data = d, random = rnd)
}

# ---- Wald chi-square test of each model term (all its coefficients jointly) ------
wald_terms <- function(a) {
  asg  <- attr(a$X, "assign")
  labs <- attr(terms(a$ff), "term.labels")
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(labs), function(k) {
    i <- which(asg == k)
    b <- a$fit$table[i, "Estimates"]
    V <- a$fit$cov[i, i, drop = FALSE]
    W <- as.numeric(t(b) %*% solve(V, b))
    data.frame(Term = labs[k], df = length(i), Chisq = W,
               p = pchisq(W, length(i), lower.tail = FALSE))
  }))
}

# ---- Model-based marginal means and pairwise contrasts ----------------------------
# Reference grid of all factor combinations; the linear combination for a group
# is the mean of its grid rows (equal weights over the remaining factors).
marginal_L <- function(a, by, at = NULL, at_level = NULL) {
  vars <- all.vars(a$ff)
  grid <- expand.grid(lapply(a$data[vars], levels), KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE)
  for (v in vars) grid[[v]] <- factor(grid[[v]], levels = levels(a$data[[v]]))
  Xg <- model.matrix(a$ff, grid)
  sel <- if (is.null(at)) rep(TRUE, nrow(grid)) else grid[[at]] == at_level
  t(vapply(levels(a$data[[by]]), function(l) colMeans(Xg[sel & grid[[by]] == l, , drop = FALSE]),
           numeric(ncol(Xg))))
}

lincom <- function(fit, L) {
  r <- betta_lincom(fit, L)
  p <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(r$`p-values`))
  p[is.na(p)] <- 0                                 # " < 1e-20"
  data.frame(estimate = r$Estimates, se = r$`Standard Errors`,
             lower = r$`Lower CIs`, upper = r$`Upper CIs`, p = p)
}

# Compact letters; level names are replaced by safe tokens because
# multcompLetters splits comparison names at "-".
cld_letters <- function(lv, pairs_df) {
  tok <- setNames(paste0("g", seq_along(lv)), lv)
  pv  <- setNames(pairs_df$p_BH, paste(tok[pairs_df$group1], tok[pairs_df$group2], sep = "-"))
  let <- multcompView::multcompLetters(pv, threshold = 0.05)$Letters
  setNames(let[tok], lv)
}

# Pairwise differences between levels of `by` within each level of `at`
# (default: treatments within compartments). BH adjustment and letters are
# computed within each compartment. Returns list(means, pairwise).
pairwise_alpha <- function(a, by = "Treatment", at = "Compartment") {
  ats <- if (at %in% names(a$data) && usable(at, a$data)) levels(a$data[[at]]) else NA
  res <- lapply(ats, function(al) {
    L  <- marginal_L(a, by, if (is.na(al)) NULL else at, al)
    lv <- rownames(L)
    means <- do.call(rbind, lapply(lv, function(l) data.frame(group = l, lincom(a$fit, L[l, ]))))
    prs <- combn(lv, 2, simplify = FALSE)
    pw  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(prs, function(pr) {
      data.frame(group1 = pr[1], group2 = pr[2], lincom(a$fit, L[pr[1], ] - L[pr[2], ]))
    }))
    pw$p_BH   <- p.adjust(pw$p, "BH")
    means$cld <- unname(cld_letters(lv, pw)[means$group])
    means$Compartment <- pw$Compartment <- if (is.na(al)) "All" else al
    list(means = means, pairwise = pw)
  })
  list(means    = do.call(rbind, lapply(res, `[[`, "means")),
       pairwise = do.call(rbind, lapply(res, `[[`, "pairwise")))
}
```

```{r betta-run, results = "asis"}
alpha_models <- list()
for (nm in unique(alpha$Set)) for (ix in c("shannon", "simpson")) {
  d  <- alpha[Set == nm & Index == ix]
  a  <- fit_alpha(d)
  wt <- wald_terms(a)
  ph <- if (usable("Treatment", a$data)) pairwise_alpha(a) else NULL
  key <- paste(nm, ix, sep = "_")
  alpha_models[[key]] <- list(model = a, wald = wt, posthoc = ph)

  save_table(wt, paste0("betta_terms_", key))
  print(ktab(wt, sprintf("%s, %s diversity: Wald tests of model terms (betta%s).",
                         nm, ix, if (a$random) "_random, Location random" else "")))
  if (!is.null(ph)) {
    pw <- ph$pairwise; mn <- ph$means
    save_table(pw, paste0("betta_pairwise_", key)); save_table(mn, paste0("betta_means_", key))
    print(ktab(pw[, c("Compartment", "group1", "group2", "estimate", "se", "p", "p_BH")],
               sprintf("%s, %s: pairwise treatment differences within compartments.", nm, ix)))
    alpha_models[[key]]$means <- mn
  }
}
```

```{r alpha-plot, eval = DO_PLOTS, fig.height = 8, fig.cap = "DivNet alpha diversity: per-sample estimates (points) and model-based treatment means within compartments (± 95 % CI) with compact letters (BH, alpha = 0.05)."}
plot_alpha <- function(nm, ix) {
  d  <- alpha[Set == nm & Index == ix]
  mn <- alpha_models[[paste(nm, ix, sep = "_")]]$means
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(Treatment, estimate, colour = Treatment)) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 1), alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_for(levels(meta$Treatment)), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste(tools::toTitleCase(ix), "(DivNet)"), title = paste(nm, "-", ix))
  if (!is.null(mn)) {
    mn$Treatment <- factor(mn$group, levels = levels(meta$Treatment))
    if (usable("Compartment", meta)) mn$Compartment <- factor(mn$Compartment, levels = levels(meta$Compartment))
    else mn$Compartment <- NULL
    p <- p +
      geom_pointrange(data = mn, aes(y = estimate, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                      colour = "black", size = 0.35) +
      geom_text(data = mn, aes(y = upper, label = cld), colour = "black",
                vjust = -0.6, size = 3.5)
  }
  if (usable("Compartment", meta)) p <- p + facet_wrap(~ Compartment, nrow = 1)
  p
}
panels <- unlist(lapply(unique(alpha$Set), function(nm)
  lapply(c("shannon", "simpson"), function(ix) plot_alpha(nm, ix))), recursive = FALSE)
save_plot(cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = panels, ncol = 2, align = "hv"),
          "alpha_divnet", height = 4 * ceiling(length(panels) / 2))
```
